text.p: Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo welcomed on Tuesday a Franco-German pledge to drive European integration ahead, quashing domestic criticism that such a stand weakened his country's position as EU president.
"I love the idea that France and the Germans are playing engine...there is nothing wrong with what happened yesterday, it has to be applauded," he told a news conference during a visit to Denmark.
"There was an idea that an attack on the Dutch presidency took place, which is absolutely not true. I was informed before and I encouraged them," he added.
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel and France's Herve de Charette told a joint news conference in Brussels on Monday their two countries were committed to being Europe's engine.
Dutch broadcast media described the Franco-German move as a slap in the face for the presidency and spoke of a "coup against the Dutch".

"The actions of France and Germany...undermine the Dutch presidency and are characteristic of the crass way in which the large member states within the European Union ignore the smaller ones," Frans Weisglas, foreign affairs spokesman for the ruling Liberal VVD coalition party, told Reuters.
Van Mierlo said that after increasing press reports of Franco-German disagreement recently, representatives of both countries told him that they intended to make a joint public stand on integration.
"I said, 'that's okay, I'm fine with it'," Van Mierlo said.
Weisglas said he would press Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok openly to reprimand France and Germany for their behaviour.
